disease_label_per_paper: Spinal epidural abscess caused by community-acquired ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae
presentation_summary: 55-year-old woman presented with fever, dysuria, malaise, urinary incontinence, and difficulty ambulating due to worsening back pain for one week.
She appeared acutely ill and diaphoretic, with temperature 38.3 degC, blood pressure 186/82 mmHg, pulse 114/min, respiratory rate 20/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.

Repeat neurologic examination after worsening mentation showed generalized weakness with diminished strength, tone, and sensation in all extremities, absent patellar reflexes, nuchal rigidity, and moderate tenderness along the entire spine.

Emergent spine MRI showed extensive posterior epidural fluid collection with internal air locules from C1 to L4, mass effect on the cord, and severe thecal sac stenosis in low cervical and mid thoracic levels.
Admission blood and urine cultures initially showed gram-negative bacilli; final blood, urine, and abscess cultures isolated ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
